report.clinical_summary: Patient with CLL diagnosed 2 years ago, currently in watch-and-wait phase with regular 3-month monitoring. Reports increased tiredness after work for several months and a new neck lump noticed by wife. Generally trying to maintain normalcy while staying vigilant about changes. Trusts doctor but wants to stay informed and maintain control.

evidence.quote: I think of CLL as something that's affecting my body's immune system cells, causing them to grow abnormally and form clusters. Even though this might not be hurting me right now, it could potentially develop into a more serious condition down the line if left unchecked.
Day to day, having CLL means being vigilant about any changes in my health and keeping up with regular appointments to monitor my blood count.
It's also made me appreciate the importance of living life fully and making each moment count, as I've had this reality check on how short life can be at times.
It's been a bit of a challenge adjusting to the idea that this is something I'll be dealing with for a while
